summary.title: Conventional Commits 1.0.0
summary.one_liner: Learn the Conventional Commits format (type, optional scope, description, body, footers, and "!" or BREAKING CHANGE markers) and how it maps commit messages to SemVer releases and changelogs.
keywords: how to write git commit messages
takeaways: Commit messages follow the pattern '<type>[optional scope]: <description>', then optional body and footers.
fix commits map to PATCH, feat commits to MINOR, and any commit with BREAKING CHANGE (or a '!' after the type/scope) to MAJOR.
Types other than feat and fix are allowed, e.g. docs, chore, build, ci, refactor, perf, test, and they have no SemVer effect unless marked breaking.
Use the squash-merge workflow or git rebase -i if contributors don't follow the spec or pick the wrong type.
summary.summary: This is the official specification page for Conventional Commits 1.0.0, a lightweight convention for structuring Git commit messages. It defines the message structure, the required and optional elements (type, scope, description, body, footers), and the rules for marking breaking changes with a footer or a '!' marker. It shows examples and explains how the convention aligns with Semantic Versioning and tooling such as automatic changelog generation. The FAQ covers practical questions on initial development, mixed-type commits, squash workflows, mistaken types, and reverts.
